# Designing for Production

Shipping a tool to thousands of developers or deploying it inside enterprise CI/CD pipelines requires high-reliability engineering: respecting signal interrupts, supporting machine-readable output formats, and managing resource consumption.

## Signal Handling and Graceful Shutdown

When an operator terminates a running utility with `Ctrl+C` (SIGINT) or Kubernetes sends SIGTERM, the process must clean up temporary files, flush write buffers, and restore the terminal state:

```toml
[dependencies]
ctrlc = "3.4"
```

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::thread;
use std::time::Duration;

fn main() {
    let running = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(true));
    let r = running.clone();

    ctrlc::set_handler(move || {
        eprintln!("\nInterrupted! Cleaning up before exit...");
        r.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }).expect("Error setting Ctrl-C handler");

    while running.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
    }

    println!("Graceful shutdown complete.");
}
```

## Machine-Readable Output: The `--json` Contract

Every production CLI should support both human-friendly formatted terminal output and structured machine-readable JSON for scripting and automation:

```rust
use clap::{Parser, ValueEnum};
use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(ValueEnum, Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum OutputFormat {
    Human,
    Json,
    Yaml,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Report {
    status: String,
    elapsed_ms: u64,
    errors_count: usize,
}

fn emit_report(report: &Report, format: OutputFormat) {
    match format {
        OutputFormat::Human => {
            println!("Status:       {}", report.status);
            println!("Duration:     {}ms", report.elapsed_ms);
            println!("Errors found: {}", report.errors_count);
        }
        OutputFormat::Json => {
            let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(report).unwrap();
            println!("{json}");
        }
        OutputFormat::Yaml => {
            // let yaml = serde_yaml::to_string(report).unwrap();
            // println!("{yaml}");
        }
    }
}
```

## Respecting `NO_COLOR` and Terminal Detection

Follow the community [no-color.org](https://no-color.org) specification:
- If `NO_COLOR` environment variable is set, disable ANSI styling.
- If stdout is not an interactive TTY (e.g., piped to a file: `mycli > out.txt`), disable ANSI colors automatically.
- Crate crates like `colored` or `anstream` respect these conventions automatically.
